x-uikit.intent: Show one or more sections at a time, collapsing the rest to their headers.
typical_uses: A list of independent sections (FAQ, settings groups) too long to show all at once, where the user opens what is relevant
Progressive disclosure of grouped content under named headers

invariants.text: With `multiple` at its default of false, opening one item closes any other open item - at most one item is open at a time.

Every `AccordionItem`'s `value` must be unique within THIS root. Nesting an `Accordion` inside another's panel needs its own value namespace: Base UI scopes keyboard navigation to the nearest root, but not value uniqueness across roots.

anti_patterns.dont: Put an always-visible required form control inside a collapsed panel
anti_patterns.instead: Keep required fields outside the accordion, or default that item's panel open - a screen reader user tabbing through the page will not discover a hidden required field until they expand that section

anti_patterns.dont: Nest an Accordion inside another Accordion's panel without checking value uniqueness across both
anti_patterns.instead: Give every item, across both roots, a unique `value`

good.title: Two sections, single-expansion (the default)
good.code:
<Accordion>
  <AccordionItem value="item-1">
    <AccordionTrigger>Is it accessible?</AccordionTrigger>
    <AccordionContent>Yes. It adheres to the WAI-ARIA design pattern.</AccordionContent>
  </AccordionItem>
  <AccordionItem value="item-2">
    <AccordionTrigger>Is it styled?</AccordionTrigger>
    <AccordionContent>Yes, with the kit's own tokens.</AccordionContent>
  </AccordionItem>
</Accordion>

bad.title: A single section used as a show/hide toggle
bad.why: One section is not what an accordion is for - it carries Base UI's multi-item expansion machinery for nothing to coordinate. Reach for `Collapsible` instead.

dont_use_when.rule: A single show/hide toggle for one piece of content
Primary navigation between sections that stays visible

assumptions.claim: value, defaultValue and onValueChange are typed in terms of a generic Value parameter
assumptions.reason: JSON Schema has no notion of a generic type parameter, so these stay annotation-only (slots) in the compiled contract rather than typed properties. accordion.md's own example uses string values (value="item-1"), which is the documented usage.
